pages.title: The event record
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Operations timeline · simulated source
pages.subject: Opening and sound check
paragraphs: The event began twelve minutes after its scheduled start. Some guests had arrived before the doors were due to open. The sound test had not been completed before admission. These three observations appear in the event log, but the log does not identify who knew about the incomplete test or when that information became available.

One proposed explanation is that the schedule left too little time for preparation. Another is that a warning was not routed to someone who could change the opening decision. The review team has not yet checked the message record. Neither explanation should be described as the established root cause at this stage.

pages.title: A participant’s account
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Participant interview · simulated source
pages.subject: What the delay felt like
paragraphs: A participant remembers waiting near the entrance and hearing different explanations from different volunteers. One person said the programme would begin soon; another said there was a technical check. The participant cannot identify who made the opening decision and does not know whether the volunteers had received the same information.

From the participant’s perspective, an accurate short update would have helped more than several confident but inconsistent estimates. This account is evidence about the participant’s experience, not proof that anyone deliberately concealed a warning. The review needs to connect the experience with the operational record before assigning responsibility or choosing a prevention.

pages.title: What was foreseeable?
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Had we known the sound test hadn’t happened, we could have held the doors for a few minutes
lines.audioText: Had we known the sound test hadn’t happened, we could have held the doors for a few minutes.
lines.translation: Se soubéssemos que o teste de som não tinha acontecido, poderíamos ter atrasado a abertura por alguns minutos

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Possibly, but did anyone have that information before the guests arrived?
lines.audioText: Possibly, but did anyone have that information before the guests arrived?
lines.translation: Talvez, mas alguém tinha essa informação antes de os convidados chegarem?

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: The timeline only says the test wasn’t completed. It doesn’t say who knew
lines.audioText: The timeline only says the test wasn’t completed. It doesn’t say who knew.
lines.translation: A linha do tempo só diz que o teste não foi concluído. Não informa quem sabia

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Then I’d avoid calling it an ignored warning until we check the message record
lines.audioText: Then I’d avoid calling it an ignored warning until we check the message record.
lines.translation: Então eu evitaria chamar de aviso ignorado antes de conferir o registro das mensagens

questions.prompt: What does the timeline establish about the sound test?
questions.answer: The timeline establishes that the test was incomplete, not who knew
They haven’t checked whether anyone received an actionable warning
Ana proposes checking the message record

pages.title: Test the explanation
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Fair. We do know the event started twelve minutes late and some guests arrived before opening
lines.audioText: Fair. We do know the event started twelve minutes late and some guests arrived before opening.
lines.translation: É justo. Sabemos que o evento começou com doze minutos de atraso e alguns convidados chegaram antes da abertura

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Those are outcomes, not necessarily the root cause of each other
lines.audioText: Those are outcomes, not necessarily the root cause of each other.
lines.translation: Esses são resultados, não necessariamente a causa um do outro

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What would distinguish a planning problem from a communication problem?
lines.audioText: What would distinguish a planning problem from a communication problem?
lines.translation: O que distinguiria um problema de planejamento de um de comunicação?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Whether there was time for the test, and whether an actionable warning reached a responsible person
lines.audioText: Whether there was time for the test, and whether an actionable warning reached a responsible person.
lines.translation: Se havia tempo para o teste e se um aviso útil chegou a alguém responsável

questions.prompt: Why don’t those outcomes establish the root cause?
questions.answer: The outcomes don’t show whether scheduling or communication failed

questions.prompt: What evidence would distinguish the two problems?
questions.answer: They need to establish whether testing time was sufficient and a responsible person received a warning

pages.title: A prevention with an owner
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: So we need to check both instead of choosing the most convenient explanation
lines.audioText: So we need to check both instead of choosing the most convenient explanation.
lines.translation: Então precisamos conferir ambos em vez de escolher a explicação mais conveniente

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Exactly. An earlier checkpoint might help, but only if someone owns the decision it triggers
lines.audioText: Exactly. An earlier checkpoint might help, but only if someone owns the decision it triggers.
lines.translation: Exatamente. Uma conferência anterior pode ajudar, mas só se alguém for responsável pela decisão resultante

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: If we do this again, I’d name that person and define when they can delay opening
lines.audioText: If we do this again, I’d name that person and define when they can delay opening.
lines.translation: Se fizermos de novo, eu definiria essa pessoa e quando ela pode atrasar a abertura

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That’s a specific prevention we can test, while keeping the causal claim provisional
lines.audioText: That’s a specific prevention we can test, while keeping the causal claim provisional.
lines.translation: É uma prevenção específica que podemos testar, mantendo a afirmação causal provisória

pages.title: Run a useful review
pages.instruction: Review what happened and agree on one change for next time

pages.title: A warning existed, but who owned it?
pages.instruction: Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I found the missing message record. A warning that the sound test was incomplete was sent before the planned opening time, but it went to a shared group without a named person responsible for responding. There’s no acknowledgement in the record. That makes a communication failure more plausible than simply saying nobody noticed a problem. It still doesn’t establish whether enough testing time had been scheduled, or whether a recipient read the warning and chose not to act. Could you revise the review to reflect that distinction? I’d like one preventive action linked to what we can actually establish, rather than a general instruction to be more careful. If you use “Had we known”, please make clear whose knowledge you mean
